observation.visible_scene: A red commuter train/tram is stopped at an outdoor platform beneath overhead catenary wires. On the left a pole-mounted orange LED timetable display and a traffic-style signal are visible. In the foreground a man in a blue jacket with grey shoulders and a dark beanie stands with his back to the camera, his right arm stretched out toward the train's open passenger door. Behind him a man in a grey shirt with a backpack waits at the same doorway, and several other pedestrians are present on the platform. The train body, windows and door frame fill the right half of the view.
visible_changes: A small red indicator light above the door area is dark in the first frames and becomes illuminated from around t=0.33s onward and stays lit.
The blue-jacketed man holds his right arm extended toward the door edge for most of the clip (t=0 to about t=1.6s), then lowers it to his side by t=1.75s and keeps it down for the remainder.
The grey-shirted man advances from behind the blue-jacketed man toward the open doorway during the middle of the clip.

A bright yellow bag is seen at the doorway from about t=1.5s and moves into the train, and later a red bag appears at the same doorway from about t=3.0s onward, indicating passengers boarding through the open door.

Pedestrians on the left platform shift position: a person in a dark jacket and cap is seen at the left edge early on, and a person in a black hooded jacket enters the left foreground later in the clip.
The overall framing of the train and background stays fixed, consistent with a stationary camera rather than train motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the train subsequently departs or the doors close.
What prompted the foreground man to extend and then lower his arm (e.g., pressing a door button, holding the door, or simply resting).
The identities of the people carrying the yellow and red bags and whether they are boarding or alighting.
Events before t=0 and after the last frame.
uncertain_details: The exact reason the red light turns on is not observable.
It is unclear whether the yellow and red objects are bags carried by boarding passengers or reflections/other items at the doorway.
Minor apparent position shifts of the train edge could be slight camera jitter rather than train movement; the background evidence is too sparse to confirm camera motion definitively.
